headline_finding.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
headline_finding.statement: the 8 children are not 8 independent walks. Within each root, the top-8 representatives sharing that root are literal prefixes of a single deterministic literal walk, differing only in which offset an available R-kind edge (w3:120, ell=5) is taken instead of declined. Across roots, a shorter shared prefix exists (the completer plus three more steps) before the walk itself begins to differ by root.

divergence_types.type_1_forced_divergence: the literal walk differs between roots because a specific continuation is illegal for one root's state (e.g. its own earlier prefix already touched the target hexagon) -- not a choice, verified forced at D1 by direct replay
divergence_types.type_2_r_admission_choice: within one root's shared walk, a legal R-kind edge becomes available as an alternative to continuing Z2/Z3 preparation; taking it yields one child (with that macro_index as its R1), declining it continues the walk toward the next such point

section_2_D1_replay_verification.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
section_2_D1_replay_verification.method: built short_root(ell) for ell in {1,2,3,4} via src/analyze_rr_short_root_envelope.py's own function, replayed each root's first 7 literal macro edges deterministically via exact.extend, then enumerated the complete fixed legal-edge set from that single state via macro.macro_edges (exhaustive rotation-run x nonrotation-joint enumeration) -- no further step taken, no branching search

short_ell3.note: both Z3 options illegal -- hex3 already visited by short_ell3's own prefix at offset -3

short_ell4.note: w2:10->hex1 is entirely absent (exact.extend returns None) -- illegal for short_ell4's specific state, not merely undesired

section_2_D1_replay_verification.conclusion: no R-kind edge exists anywhere in this 19/19/21/21-edge enumeration for any of the four roots -- D1 is a purely Z2/Z3 structural fork, unrelated to R-admission, and short_ell4's divergence there is forced, not a free choice. This directly refutes reading D1 as a 'registration repair' opportunity (task 4) -- there was nothing to repair.

claim_A.text: the first five spine transitions are conjugate across roots
claim_A.true_for: completer plus offsets 1-3 (4 transitions), with only the offset-1 rotation length varying as the proven 4-root_ell parameter
claim_A.false_at: the fifth transition (offset 4): short_ell4 takes Z3;w3:201->hex3 instead of the other three roots' Z2;w2:10->hex1 -- a different joint KIND, not a parameter variant, and forced by illegality (section 2)
claim_A.exact_counterpattern: short_ell4's offset-4 edge vs the shared group's offset-4 edge, per section_1 D1 record

claim_B.text: the only root-dependent parameter is the final rotation length
counterpatterns: the completer's own source AND target orbit/phase differ by root, not merely a rotation length
D1: short_ell4's divergence is a joint-kind substitution (Z2->Z3), not a rotation-length variant
D2 and D3 are likewise joint-kind substitutions between siblings sharing an otherwise-identical prefix
claim_B.note: the 4-root_ell rotation-length identity at offset 1 remains correct and clean, but is not the only root-dependent quantity

claim_C.text: every legal R alternative before the first divergence targets an orbit different from the required future R2 source orbit
claim_C.finding: in every checked instance the R-alternative and the declined continuation target the IDENTICAL orbit, differing only in phase -- the claim as literally stated (different orbit) is false at every point checked. A weaker phase-sensitive restatement would be true in the same instances but was not what was asked.
claim_C.additional_note: no R-kind edge exists at or before D1 at all, so the claim is vacuous in that window and was instead evaluated at the Type-2 (R-admission) branch points

claim_D.text: registering the required orbit necessarily changes the future R2 source
claim_D.reasoning: once a joint move is taken at a given state it consumes the step and determines the next state by construction -- any two different moves at the same state necessarily lead to different subsequent walks and different sourceable orbits. True essentially by definition of a single-edge-per-step literal walk, not a fact specific to R2 geometry or registration.
claim_D.grade: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION, not promoted to a substantive theorem

claim_E.text: any path preserving the required future source cannot merge the needed components before R2
claim_E.evidence: in all 8 checked children, R1's own target orbit sits in an isolated single-orbit component, never merged with the hub component, regardless of how far along the spine R1 fired (offsets 41 to 58 -- up to 17 further preparation edges of delay did not change the outcome in any of the 8 cases)
claim_E.caveat: n=8, not exhaustive; no general argument given for why this would hold beyond the sample checked

section_4_r1_target_isolation.label: CLAUDE_HAND_PROOF
section_4_r1_target_isolation.method: for each of the 8 children, located the incidence_forest component containing hub.id (always 0) and the component containing R1_geometry.target_orbit, directly from each child's own JSON record -- no computation beyond membership lookup
section_4_r1_target_isolation.result: in all 8 of 8 children, R1's target-orbit component is different from the hub component, and is always minimal (e_orbits=1, hexagons=2 or 3)
section_4_r1_target_isolation.significance: this is the exact, quantitative form of the 'source-orbit registration barrier' described qualitatively two rounds ago -- now confirmed uniformly across the full top-8 set, not just asserted by analogy to short_ell0

section_5_smallest_unresolved_template.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL -- open question, precisely stated, not resolved
section_5_smallest_unresolved_template.template: Does there exist, from R1's target orbit/phase, any legal Z2/Z3 continuation -- within the remaining resource budget (1 further R event, hub_touch_count <= 2, F_def == 1, H == 0) -- whose own orbit registration merges R1's target-orbit component with the component that will contain the eventual R2 target orbit (in particular, with the hub component, since every checked R2 candidate's target orbit traces back toward hex 0's territory)?
section_5_smallest_unresolved_template.grounding: derived directly from target_a_recognizer's exact same_component(source,target) requirement (verified from source two rounds ago, reused unchanged) and section_4's uniform finding
section_5_smallest_unresolved_template.status: genuinely open; not answered by any data inspected this round or prior rounds; not attempted by search here, per task instruction
section_5_smallest_unresolved_template.relation_to_prior_finding: the same underlying question as the single-legal-continuation lookahead evidence-need identified two rounds ago for the single-successor children, now given exact symbolic form in terms of incidence_components and the recognizer's own same_component predicate
